title: Wes Helvey's band in Cincinnati and Leonard Gay
summary: After Madison he played in Cincinnati with Wes Helvey, then returned to Wisconsin with saxophonist Leonard Gay, a Trumbauer devotee.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We left off where you came back home and you decided to learn to read, and then you went out again.
It was Madison where I decided to learn to read -- and write. But I did go back out again, but I had played with several other guys that... I played with a band called Helvey in Cincinnati.
Yeah, Wes Helvey. You know about him, eh?
Well, I've looked it up. I've been doing a little research.

Yeah. He had a good band. A very good band. Then...Helvey... Then after Helvey, I went back out there. I went back out to Wisconsin. In that band, it was Leonard Gay who was in it... That's him; that's his picture up there. Look, there's the Speed Webb band. He's the tenor(?) saxophone player, the one in the middle -- Leonard Gay. He just died, I understand, a couple...about a month or two ago -- after all this time. So he was a... He was a very good saxophone player. He sounded a lot like Frankie Trumbauer. He copied Frankie. He was crazy about Frankie Trumbauer. So he would play all them solos of Frankie's, and things like that.
